The root-approved relay observation fault is explicit and narrow: after first
accepted/lost send, return unavailable only for `getrawtransaction(A-txid,1)`
until the original parent has fully joined. This prevents the autonomous
scheduler from confirming A before the restart boundary. It does not alter node
state, transaction bytes, wallet signing or other RPCs. Record its match/count
and release before starting the CLI; no fault remains during child recovery.

Daily authenticated Balance and PayoutsPage are inspected through actual TLS.
Before recovery the Gym1 page exposes the original reserved payment; afterward
it exposes that same confirmed payment and Gym2 has an empty done page with its
full dated balance. Bind source, settlement, recipient, gym and capture fields;
page sums never substitute for total balances. Empty/nonfinal multi-page history
is covered by the separate actual original-ledger18-payment test.

New main/flow/audit leaves own adaptation. The existing node helper is copied
with provenance; root owns the outer execution wrapper. Public artifacts retain
phase JSON, original full work/receipts, signed payment, public counts/balances/
pages, clock observations and exact process cleanup. Do not inspect wallets,
seeds or credentials after creation. Public journal audit never overlaps a live
runtime/CLI owner. Failure retains fixture roots; uncertain cleanup cannot pass.
This proves one finite two-gym public daily recovery scenario, not continuous
64-miner service, all source capacity, GUI login, deployment or real-key custody.

Root-selected audit successor: use two exact-root production --daily serve lifetimes. The first joins at B59 before the full closed-store no-lock/no-credit audit; the second begins after the one final block and joins after B60 import. No concurrent raw DB reader, extra block, changed budget or parent wallet reattachment is introduced. Original PLAN is retained.
